narrative:
The model estimates you have a 24% chance of not passing your final year, which is above the 10% threshold that requires additional support. This doesn’t mean failure is certain, but it does mean the system has identified patterns in your situation that often lead to struggling students, so you’ll need to take remedial courses to help stay on track.

The most important factor working in your favor is that you’ve never failed a class before—this significantly reduces the risk of failing this year. However, two key factors are increasing that risk. First, your father’s education level is lower than most students who aren’t required to take remedial courses, which the model associates with a higher chance of struggling. Second, you have low free time after school, which may limit opportunities to study, relax, or seek help when needed.

Other aspects of your situation, like your parents living together and your strong desire to pursue higher education, are positive signs, but they don’t outweigh the concerns above. The good news is that this isn’t a final judgment—it’s a chance to address potential challenges early. Focus on making the most of your remedial courses, finding small ways to create more study time, and leaning on your support system. With effort, you can still succeed this year.
